correctness.rationale: On the zero-sum subspace the loop-free complete-graph walk acts by −1/(n−1), so BA^k=U+r_k(B−U) in the stated column-update order. For k≥2 the product is positive because A^k is positive. For k=1, (BA)_{ij}=(1−B_{ij})/(n−1); rows of the odd-cycle vertices are positive, every row reaches one of those vertices, and all diagonal entries are positive. This gives primitivity. Products within a block preserve constants and contract the sup norm, so convergence at block endpoints gives convergence at all phases. The stationary equation gives the resolvent; the row-ℓ¹ contraction of B on signed vectors gives the stated geometric series tail and strict onset inequality. Weighted degree reversibility and uniqueness of the stationary law of B prove uB=u exactly for constant weighted degrees. In the triangle, symmetry and the third-coordinate stationary equation give π_{k,3}=1/(3+r_k); odd k gives a value above 1/3 and even k a value between 1/4 and 1/3. No general all-k or temporal-oscillation claim is needed. The supplied finite rational check was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: For a general second layer the bound is eventual, and is stated only for coordinates with nonzero first-order coefficient. The all-k overshoot comparison is specific to the triangle.

evidence: The general stationary perturbation equation is (π̃−π)(I−P+1πᵀ)=π̃(P̃−P) for normalized stationary rows, obtained by subtraction. Here P=U and the fundamental matrix is the identity.
For the published triangle, column 3 of B is (1/3,1/3,0)ᵀ and rows 1 and 2 are related by the swap symmetry.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The complete graph power is U+r_k(I−U); substitute P̃=BA^k=U+r_k(B−U) to get δ=r_k c+r_k δB for δ=π_k−u and c=uB−u. Inversion has no further graph-specific step: δ=r_k c(I−r_kB)⁻¹. The first Taylor coefficient is c, and the remainder is the ordinary row-ℓ¹ geometric majorant. Its sign test follows since r_k alternates; c=0 exactly when B has a uniform stationary law, equivalently constant weighted degrees. In the already-known triangle, the third-coordinate equation immediately gives (3+r_k)π_{k,3}=1, and comparing the denominators gives all parity inequalities. Thus both parts are direct exact consequences, though the prior switching paper reports only the unsigned bound and the initial witness explicitly.

originality.rationale: Shiu–Naghizadeh do not state the signed all-k formula or the all-large-k parity test. But the resolvent and signed leading term are a direct rank-one instance of the classical stationary perturbation identity, on the very switched product already analyzed by that paper. The threshold is the elementary tail bound on the resulting Neumann series, and the triangle is their already published k=1 witness with the same one-dimensional indeterminate r carried through its stationarity equation. This is a mechanical specialization, not an exact-duplicate claim. The conclusion does not rely on unavailable full text or on treating the prior O(ρ₂(A)^k) magnitude estimate alone as a signed one.
residual_risks: This is an implication/routineness finding, not an assertion that a prior paper prints the all-period formula. The original Schweitzer full text and alternative Cho–Meyer copies were unavailable; the elementary identity and its specialization were checked directly.

value.rationale: The distinction between a signed limit response and an unsigned convergence rate is meaningful. In this frozen complete-layer case it is exhausted by the first coefficient of the standard rank-one stationary perturbation and the already studied triangle; the onset estimate is the generic geometric remainder. There is no new nonroutine witness, wider sign theorem beyond that reduction, or independent invariant here that would support acceptance.
